title: Add event-driven RAG quickstart (SQS-triggered retrieval + Redwood Functions adapter)
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Adds a serverless RAG quickstart demonstrating SQS-triggered retrieval, background embedding refresh, and a Redwood Functions adapter for secure tool-calling; intended for customers building asynchronous retrieval pipelines.
description: Motivation: Many customers build asynchronous pipelines where retrieval and augmentation happen off the request path (e.g., background document ingestion, embedding refreshes, or queued retrieval). This quickstart provides a simple, production-minded example that ties SQS as the ingestion/trigger mechanism to a Redwood Functions adapter that performs retrieval, runs a small tool chain (caller pattern), and writes enriched responses back to a result queue; the goal is to show patterns for security, retries, idempotency, and cost-aware batching. What this PR includes: 1) examples/event-driven-rag/README.md with architecture diagram, operational checklist, and rollout notes; 2) a minimal Redwood Functions adapter (examples/event-driven-rag/functions/adapter.ts) demonstrating model selection, structured output, and function/tool calling patterns; 3) a sample SQS consumer (examples/event-driven-rag/consumer/worker.py) for teams preferring Python; 4) terraform snippets for an optional quick infra setup (examples/event-driven-rag/infra/README.tf); 5) test harness and local emulation instructions (examples/event-driven-rag/test/README.md) and CI job to run the worker integration tests. Checklist: - [x] architecture doc and failure modes section; - [x] secure env var patterns and KMS hints; - [x] example code in TS and Python; - [x] CI job that runs integration against LocalStack; - [x] docs site link and quickstart registration. Usage notes: The README walks through a local dev flow using LocalStack + docker-compose, how to seed a document into S3 + SQS, expected message schema, and how to observe outputs. Operational guidance includes idempotency key best practices, recommended batch sizes for Redis/KV cache hits, fallback policy to smaller models when large instance capacity not available, and cost guardrails for background embedding refresh. Related work and tickets: ENG-3210 (RAG background workflows), PM-145 (quickstart prioritization), SUP-88 (support case that motivated the retry recommendations). Migration and compatibility: Not a breaking change; code samples are additive. Security: examples include a minimal KMS usage snippet and notes for VPC/private deployments. How to review: start with README.md and the Functions adapter; run LocalStack integration test locally or rely on CI. Review notes in this PR capture an approval path and two small follow-ups (doc wording and a lint quirk fixed).
